title: Meningococcal meningitis in Cascavel triggers alert at day care center
seoTitle: Meningitis Case in Cascavel Prompts Daycare Alert
subtitle: confirmed case in 4-year-old child leads to parade withdrawal and distribution of preventive medication
excerpt: A case of meningococcal meningitis was confirmed in a 4-year-old child in Cascavel, prompting immediate prevention and control measures.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A case of meningococcal meningitis was confirmed in a 4-year-old child at the Cmei Doce Infância day care center in Cascavel, triggering immediate prevention and control measures by Epidemiological Surveillance.

confirmed case in 4-year-old child

The confirmation was released on Friday (4) by the municipal health and education departments. The child, enrolled at Cmei Doce Infância in the Cataratas neighborhood, is the first confirmed case in the region.

prevention and control measures

Following the identification of the case, Epidemiological Surveillance initiated actions outlined in disease prevention and control protocols. Among them is the containment of close contacts, aimed at reducing the risk of new cases and breaking a potential chain of transmission.

preventive medication for close contacts

Students identified as close contacts will receive Rifampicin, along with a prescription and instructions for proper use. The measure follows established guidelines for confirmed cases of meningococcal disease. The team in charge is evaluating each contact and delivering the medication, which must be administered as directed.

cancellation of September 7 parade participation

As a preventive measure, Cmei Doce Infância will not participate in the September 7 parade. The Department of Education stated that the school reported the case as soon as it became aware of the situation and that measures are being implemented jointly with the Department of Health.

guidance for families and on-call surveillance

Families will receive materials containing information about symptoms and care related to the disease. Epidemiological Surveillance maintains an on-call service available for guidance at (45) 98431-6339. Emergency Care Unit (UPA) teams have also been briefed and are prepared to receive children if necessary.

recommendations for parents and guardians

Parents and guardians should monitor children's health status and seek medical attention if symptoms or health changes appear. The guidance is to follow the recommendations provided by Epidemiological Surveillance, with no need for a widespread suspension of school activities.

With information from O Paraná.
